** ** **
 Common Judgment

These petitions were filed by the petitioner
claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ and
Rs.10,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by them in
the road traffic accident caused on 29.05.2019.
 02.

Hence these petitions were clubbed together
for the purpose of recording common evidence.

The
main petition is M.V.C.No.4798/2019 and it is clubbed
with M.V.C.No.4799/19.
 03.

The brief facts in M.V.C.No.4798/2019 is
as under:

It is submitted that on 29.05.2019 at about
09.15 p.m when the petitioner was driving Auto
bearing No.KA42A4610 along with passengers on
the extreme left side of Mangaluru - Bengaluru Nh75
Road, near Bus Stand, Rasthepalya, Thippasandra
Hobli, Ramanagara, at that time suddenly the driver of
Lorry bearing No.KA13D7999 came from behind, in
rash and negligent manner and dashed against the
auto.

Due to this the auto turtle and petitioner along
In: Sri.M.N.Shivakumara vs In: 01. Sri.Sudharshan on 21 January, 2023
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149625881/
2

 (Scch3) 4 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
with inmates have sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was
shifted to Kunigal Government hospital and after first
aid he was referred to Victoria hospital, wherein due to
nonavailability of Surgeon he was again shifted to
Sanjay Gandhi hospital and was admitted as inpatient
and has undergone surgery.

The petitioner had spent
more than Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical expenses
and other incidental charges.

The petitioner prior to
the accident was hale and healthy and was Auto driver
by profession and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m. Due to the
accident till today he cannot attend his work and
sustained disability and lost his earning capacity.

The
accident occurred due to the negligence of the
offending Lorry driver only.

Even a criminal case is
registered against the said lorry driver. The respondent
No.1 is the R.C. Owner and the respondent No.2 is the
insurer of the said lorry.

Hence both respondents are
jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to
the petitioners.
Hence this petition.

04. The brief facts in M.V.C.No.4799/2019 is
as under:

It is submitted that on 29.05.2019 at about
09.15 p.m when the petitioner was proceeding in Auto
bearing No.KA42A4610 as passenger and the same
 (Scch3) 5 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
was driven by petitioner in M.V.C.No.4798/2019, on
the extreme left side of Mangaluru - Bengaluru Nh75
Road, near Bus Stand, Rasthepalya, Thippasandra
Hobli, Ramanagara, at that time suddenly the driver of
Lorry bearing No.KA13D7999 came from behind, in
rash and negligent manner and dashed against the
auto.

Due to this the auto turtle and petitioner along
with driver and other inmates have sustained grievous
injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner
was shifted to Kunigal Government hospital and after
first aid he was referred to Victoria hospital, wherein
due to nonavailability of Surgeon again he was shifted
to Sanjay Gandhi hospital and was admitted as
inpatient and has undergone surgery.

The petitioner
had spent more than Rs.2,50,000/ towards medical
expenses and other incidental charges.

The petitioner
prior to the accident was hale and healthy and was
doing fruits vending business and earning Rs.20,000/
p.m.

Due to the accident till today he cannot attend
his work and sustained disability and lost his earning

capacity.

The accident occurred due to the negligence
of the offending Lorry driver only.

Even a criminal case
is registered against the said lorry driver.

The
respondent No.1 is the R.C. Owner and the respondent
No.2 is the insurer of the said lorry.

Hence both
 (Scch3) 6 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the
compensation to the petitioners.
Hence this petition.

05. After service of notice, the respondents have
appeared through their counsel and filed

written
statement in both petitions.

06. The averments of the written statement of
the respondent No.1 is as under :

This respondent is the owner of the Lorry bearing
No.KA13D7999 and insured with the respondent
No.2.
The said policy was valid on the date of accident.

The driver who had drove the offending vehicle has
valid driving licence on the date of accident.

The
accident occurred due to the negligence of auto driver.

This respondent has denied the manner of accident,
injuries, treatment and income as stated by the
petitioners.

The claim of the petitioners are not
reasonable and excessive and prays to dismiss both
petitions with costs.

07. The averments of the written statement of
respondent No.2 in both petitions are as under:

The petitions are bad for nonjoinder of necessary
parties.

There is delay of 2 days in lodging the Police
complaint.

This respondent has denied issuance of
Policy with respect to the Lorry bearing No.
Ka13D7999, pending confirmation from the
 (Scch3) 7 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
concerned branch of this respondent.

But
the liability of this respondent if any, is subject to
terms and conditions of the policy.

That the offending
lorry was not involved in the accident.

The accident
took place due to the negligence of auto driver.

The
offending lorry driver was not holding valid driving
licence on the date of accident.
The respondent No.1
has not intimated about the accident.

It is denied that
due to the accident the petitioners have sustained
disability and lost income as stated in the petitions.

This respondent has denied the manner of accident,
injuries and income as stated by the petitioners.

The
claim of the petitioners are excessive and prays to
dismiss all petitions with costs.

08. In order to prove the case, the petitioners in

both petitions, Mro and the Doctor were examined
themselves as Pw.1 to 4 and got marked 28
documents as per Ex.P.1 to 28 and closed their side.

09. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2
submits no oral evidence.

The respondent No.1 did not
adduced any oral evidence.
10. Heard both sides in both petitions.

11. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the
following issues have been framed: 
 (Scch3) 8 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
 Issues In M.V.C.No.4798/2019
 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he
 has sustained injuries in the accident
 occurred on 29.05.2019 at about 09.15 p.m on
 Mangaluru - Bengaluru Nh75 Road, near Bus
 Stand, Rasthepalya, Thippasandra Hobli,
 Ramanagara, due to rash and negligent act of
 the driving of the Lorry bearing registration
 No.KA13D7999 by its driver as alleged in
 the petition?
 02.

Whether the petitioner is entitled for
 compensation?

If so, to what amount & from
 whom?
 03.
What order or award?

Issues In M.V.C.No.4799/2019
 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he
 has sustained injuries in the accident
 occurred on 29.05.2019 at about 09.15 p.m on
 Mangaluru - Bengaluru Nh75 Road, near Bus
 Stand, Rasthepalya, Thippasandra Hobli,
 Ramanagara, due to rash and negligent act of
 the driving of the Lorry bearing registration
 No.KA13D7999 by its driver as alleged in
 the petition?

02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for
 compensation?

If so, to what amount & from
 whom?
( Scch3
What order or award?

 12.

My findings on the aforesaid issues are as
under:
 Issues In M.V.C.No.4798/2019
 Issue No.1 :
In affirmative
Issue No.2 :

In partly affirmative
 Issue No.3 :

As per final order
 for the following:
 Issues In M.V.C.No.4799/2019
 Issue No.1 : In affirmative
 Issue No.2 : In partly affirmative
 Issue No.3 : As per final order
 for the following:
 Reasons
 13.

Issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.4798/19 and
issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.4799/19

: These issues will
be taken at one stretch for my consideration as they

are inter related with each other and common in order
to avoid repetition of facts.

It is the grievance of the petitioners that they
have sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and
negligent driving of Lorry bearing No.KA13D7999 by
 (Scch3) 10 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
its driver.

Due to the accident they have sustained
disability and lost income.

The same was opposed by
the respondents and contended that the accident did

not took place due to the negligence of offending lorry
driver and it is due to the negligence of auto driver.

The insured vehicle is falsely implicated in this case in
order to claim compensation.

Hence they are not liable
to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

14. To prove this, the petitioner of
M.V.C.No.4798/19 was got examined himself as Pw.1
by reiterating all the averments of the petition in his
affidavit.

The Pw.1 in his cross examination has
admitted that "On the date of accident 04 person were
proceeding in auto towards Thippasandra to bring rice.

It is true that the accident took place within the
jurisdiction of Ramanagara District.

That I was driving
the auto.
I have not produced my driving licence.

My
brother is the owner of said auto.

The lorry came and
dash me from my hind side.

I could not say the speed
of lorry as it came from my hind side.
It is true that no
In: Sri.M.N.Shivakumara vs In: 01. Sri.Sudharshan on 21 January, 2023

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149625881/
6

damages is noted down for the lorry in Imv report.
That the back portion of my auto is damaged.

I can
produce Mlc extract.

It is true that I had not produced
any documents to show that I have obtained follow up
treatment.
I have not surrendered my driving licence

(Scch3) 11 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
to Rto.

It is true that I have not produced nay
documents to show that was earning Rs.25,000/ per
month as auto driver".

Apart from this the Pw.1 had
denied other suggestion of the respondents counsel.

15. Further another injured and the claimant in
M.V.C.No.4799/2019 was got examined himself as
Pw.2 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in
his affidavit.

In his cross examination he has admitted
that "That including the driver four persons were
proceeding in the auto.

That the accident took place
on BengaluruMangaluru road.

That the said lorry came
from our behind side.

I do not know who gave
complaint to the police.

It is true that I took
conservative treatment.

Prior to the accident I was
working as fruit vendor.

I have not produced any
documents to show that I am doing fruit vending
business and earning Rs.20,000/ per month ".

Apart
from this the Pw.2 had denied all suggestion of the
respondents counsel.

16. The Pw.1 and 2 in support of their case got
marked entire police documents at Ex.P.1 to 8 and 17.

So on perusal of these documents, it is clear that the
concerned I.O after investigation has filed chargesheet
against the offending Lorry driver for the alleged
offences punishable U/Sec 279, 338 of Ipc stating that
 (Scch3) 12 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
the petitioners have sustained injuries due to rash and
negligent driving of offending Lorry driver only.
 17.

It is true that eventhough the respondents
contended that the accident does not took place due to
their insured lorry, but to prove this they have not
adduced any supportive oral and documentary
evidence.

Even the mahazar and Imv reports got
marked supports the version of the petitioners.

So on
perusal of all police records accompanied with the oral
evidence of the Pw.1 and 2 and in absence of rebuttal
evidence by the respondents in this regard, it is true
that the petitioners have proved that the offending
Lorry was involved in this accident and its driver due
to his negligent driving had caused the accident which
leads to injuries to them.
In: Sri.M.N.Shivakumara vs In: 01. Sri.Sudharshan on 21 January, 2023
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149625881/
7

 18. Therefore with the available oral and
documentary evidence, it is true that the petitioners
have proved that they have sustained injuries due to
the rash and negligent driving of the offending Lorry
driver.

Hence I answered the issue No.1 in
M.V.C.No.4798/19 in affirmative and issue No.1 in
M.V.C.No.4799/19 in affirmative.
 19.
Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.4798/19 and

issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.4799/19: These issues will be
taken at one stretch for my consideration as they are
 (Scch3) 13 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
inter related with each other and common in order to
avoid repetition of facts.

20 . Further the petitioner in M.V.C.No.4798/19
has stated that due to the accident he is not able to do
work as earlier and sustained disability.

In this regard
he has got examined the Mro as Pw.3 who had got
marked the Mlc register, Police intimation and entire
Case sheet of this petitioner as per Ex.P.19 to 21.
 21.

This petitioner has also examined the
Orthopedic Surgeon as Pw.4 who had stated that
petitioner sustained left leg degloving injury, with
multiple abrasions all over the body.

That the
petitioner complained of unable to walk normally,
unable to sit down, squat and sit crossleg.

On
examination the petitioner has walk with equinus gait,
stiff ankle, badly deformed left legs with total loss of
muscle bulk in the left leg, ankle movements absent.
Recent Xray of the left leg shows equinus ankle with
reduced left ankle joint line.

22. The Pw.4 had assessed physical disability of
the left lower limbs at 48% and 16% to whole body
physical disability.

The Pw.4 has got produced Clinical
notes and Xray as per Ex.P.25 and 26.
 23.

The Pw.4 in his cross examination has
admitted that "It is true that the injuries are healed up
 (Scch3) 14 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
with deformity.

It is true that in 2019 skin grafting was
done.

It is true that now the muscle activation are
normal.

It is true that the treatment is over for
degloving injuries.

It is true that at the time of wound
debridement and primary treatment the present xray
findings are not found.

It is true that apart from
degloving injury the petitioner has not sustained any
other fracture".
 24.

Hence, from the evidence of Pw.4 and
Ex.P.25 and 26, the assessed disability by the Pw.4
In: Sri.M.N.Shivakumara vs In: 01. Sri.Sudharshan on 21 January, 2023
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149625881/
8

cannot be taken into consideration.

Hence under these
circumstances, I just feel it proper to consider 12%
disability for the petitioner.

25 . Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the
compensation under the following heads:
 a).
Loss of future income:

The Pw.1 has
stated that he was working as auto Driver by
profession and earning Rs.25,000/ per month.

In this
regard he had not produced any documents or his
driving licence to show that he was working as auto
driver.

Hence in absence of such documents, I just feel
it proper to consider the notional income.

As on the
date of accident

the notional income can be fixed at
Rs.14,000/.

The Pw.1 had stated that he was aged
about 25 years at the time of accident.

In this regard
 (Scch3) 15 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
the Pw.1 has got marked his Aadhaar card at Ex.P.12
which shows that he was born on 01.01.1994.

So as
per Ex.P.12 the petitioner was 25 years old at the time
of accident.
Thereby proper multiplier comes to "18".

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future
income as Rs.14,000 x 12 x 18 x 12/100 =
Rs.3,62,880/ under this head.

b). Pain and sufferings during treatment
period: The petitioner has stated that he was
admitted in hospital as inpatient.

But in this regard he
had not produced any documents.

Hence under these
circumstances considering the injuries sustained by
the petitioner, I just feel it proper to award
Rs.20,000/ under this head as the petitioner might
have spent amount when he took treatment as
inpatient.

c). Towards medical expenses: The petitioner
has got marked entire medical bills and prescriptions
as per Ex.P.9, 11 and 13 which amounts to Rs.2,995/
and Rs.861/.

The petitioner also produced advance
receipts (06 in numbers) for a sum of Rs.37,000/ as
per Ex.P.10.

But in support of the said bills the
petitioner has not produced any inpatient bill or other
supportive bills.

Hence the petitioner is not entitled for
the amount paid under advance receipts.

There is no
 (Scch3) 16 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
serious dispute with regard to other medical bills
produced and marked by the petitioner.

Hence the
petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,856/ under this head.
d). Loss of income during laid up period:-
Admittedly the Pw.1 as per available records could not

In: Sri.M.N.Shivakumara vs In: 01. Sri.Sudharshan on 21 January, 2023
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149625881/
9

do any work for about 1 month after the accident.
Hence, he is entitled for Rs.14,000/ under this head.

e). Loss of amenities and nutrition food:-
The Pw.1 had not produced any documents to show
that he had incurred amount towards amenities and
nutritious food.

But looking into the period of
treatment and the nature of injuries

, I just feel it
proper to award a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this
head.

f). Towards attendent charges and
conveyance: The Pw.1 has not produced any
discharge summary to show that he took treatment as
inpatient.

It is true that the petitioner had took
treatment as outpatient.

In absence of such
documents, I just feel it proper to award a sum of
Rs.5,000/ under this head.

g). Towards future medical expenses : The
Pw.4 has stated that the petitioner needs another
surgery for the correction of the ankle deformity at the
cost of Rs.60,000/.

But in this regard no documents
 (Scch3) 17 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
were produced by the petitioner.

Hence under these
circumstances I just feel it proper to award a sum of
Rs.15,000/ under this head.

26 . Therefore, the petitioner in M.V.C.
No.4798/19 is entitled for total compensation of
Rs.4,30,736/ (Four lakhs thirty thousand seven
hundred and thirty six only).
 27.

Further the petitioner in M.V.C.No.4799/19
has stated that due to the accident he is not able to do
work as earlier and sustained disability.

In this regard
he has got examined the Mro as Pw.3 who had got
marked the Mlc register, Police intimation and entire
Case sheet of this petitioner as per Ex.P.22 to 24.
 28.

This petitioner has also examined the
Orthopedic Surgeon as Pw.4 who had stated that
petitioner sustained fracture of the left 1st metacarpal
bone.

That the petitioner complained of weakness and
pain in the left hand, unable to grip and hold objects
in the left hand and do his profession as fruit vendor.

On examination the petitioner has loss of grip in the
left hand, loss of strength in the left hand.

The recent
Xray of the left hand shows united fracture of the 1st
metacarpal.

29. The Pw.4 had assessed total physical
disability of left hand at 20% and 7% to whole body
 (Scch3) 18 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
In: Sri.M.N.Shivakumara vs In: 01. Sri.Sudharshan on 21 January, 2023

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149625881/
10

physical disability.

The Pw.4 has got produced Clinical
notes and Xray as per Ex.P.27 and 28.
 30.

The Pw.4 in his cross examination has
admitted that "It is true that I had not treated the
petitioner personally.

It is true that the petitioner
underwent Kwire fixation".
 31.

The Pw.4 has not stated about requirement
of future medical expenses and surgery for this
petitioner.

Hence this petitioner is not entitled for any
amount under the head of future medical expenses.

Hence, from the evidence of Pw.4 and Ex.P.27 and 28,
the assessed disability by the Pw.4 cannot be taken
into consideration.

Hence under these circumstances, I
just feel it proper to consider 5% disability for the
petitioner.

32. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the
compensation under the following heads:
 a).
Loss of future income:

The Pw.2 has stated
that he was Fruits Vendor by profession and earning
Rs.20,000/ per month.

In this regard he had not
produced any documents.

Hence, in the absence of
such documents, I just feel it proper to consider the
notional income.

As on the date of accident the
notional income can be fixed at Rs.14,000/.

The Pw.2
had stated that he was aged about 26 years at the time
 (Scch3) 19 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
of accident.

In this regard the Pw.2 has got marked his
Aadhaar card at Ex.P.16 which shows that he was
born on 27.01.1994.

So as per Ex.P.16 the petitioner
was 25 years old at the time of accident.

Thereby
proper multiplier comes to "18".

Therefore, the
petitioner is entitled for loss of future income as
Rs.14,000 x 12 x 18 x 5/100 = Rs.1,51,200/ under
this head.

b). Pain and sufferings during treatment
period: The petitioner has stated that he was
admitted in hospital as inpatient.

But in this regard he
had not produced any documents.

Hence under these
circumstances, I just feel it proper to award
Rs.20,000/ under this head as the petitioner might
have spent amount when he took treatment as
inpatient.

c). Towards medical expenses: The petitioner
has got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.15
which amounts to Rs.3,300/ which includes advance
receipts of Rs.3,000/.

Even this petitioner has not
produced final inpatient bill.

There is no serious
dispute with regard to other medical bills produced
and marked by the petitioner.

Hence the petitioner is
entitled for Rs.300/ under this head.

In: Sri.M.N.Shivakumara vs In: 01. Sri.Sudharshan on 21 January, 2023
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149625881/
11

 (Scch3) 20 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
 d).
Loss of income during laid up period:-

Admittedly the Pw.2 as per available records could not
do any work for about 1 month after the accident.
Hence, he is entitled for Rs.14,000/ under this head.

e). Loss of amenities and nutrition food:-
The Pw.2 had not produced any documents to show
that he had incurred amount towards amenities and
nutritious food.

But looking into the period of
treatment and the nature of injuries, I just feel it
proper to award a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this
head.

f). Towards attendent charges and
conveyance: The Pw.2 did not took treatment as
inpatient.

Even he had not produced any documents in
this regard.

Hence he might have taken treatment as
outpatient only.

In absence of documents, I just feel it
proper to award a sum of Rs.5,000/ under this head.

33. Therefore, the petitioner in M.V.C.
No.4799/19 is entitled for total compensation of
Rs.2,00,500/ (Two lakhs and five hundred only).

34. Regarding liability : The respondent No.2
from the initial stage has contended that they have not
issued policy in the name of respondent No.1 and it
created.

Hence they are not liable to pay compensation
to the petitioners.

Later the counsel for respondent
 (Scch3) 21 MVC.No.4798/19
 c/w MVC.No.4799/19
No.2 on 20012023 has filed Memo along with policy
copy which shows the respondent No.2 has issued
Package (Goods carrying (other than 3wheeler  public
carriers) policy which was valid on the date of
accident.

It is true that the petitioners have proved
that the accident occurred due to the rash and
negligent driving of the offending Lorry driver.

The said
offending lorry was owned by the respondent No.1 and
insured with respondent No.2.

Hence both
respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay
compensation to the petitioners.

Hence I answered the
issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.4798/2019 in partly
affirmative and issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.4799/2019
in partly affirmative.
 35. Issue No.3 in M.V.C.No.4798/19 and
issue No.3 in M.V.C.No.4799/19: These issues will

be taken at one stretch for my consideration as they
are inter related with each other and common in order
